# package encap

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/encap"
```

Package encap is the EtherNet/IP encapsulation codec: the 24-octet header, the commands and their status codes, the common packet format (CPF) and the items of ListIdentity, ListServices and the connected and I/O messages.

The package is a pure codec: it does no I/O beyond [ReadPacket](#func-readpacket) over an io.Reader, and keeps no state. Every decoder checks lengths against the data it is given before allocating, so it is safe on untrusted input.

```go
	CapabilityTCP uint16 = 0x0020
	// CapabilityUDP is set when the device supports CIP Class 0 and 1
	// messaging over UDP (implicit messaging).
	CapabilityUDP uint16 = 0x0100
)
```

```go
type Header struct {
```


Packet is an encapsulation packet: a header and its data.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (Packet, error)
```

Decode decodes a packet that fills b exactly, as a UDP datagram carries it. The data aliases b.

#### func ReadPacket

```go
func ReadPacket(r io.Reader, buf []byte, max int) (Packet, []byte, error)
```

ReadPacket reads one packet from a stream. buf is reused when it is large enough; the packet's data aliases the returned buffer, which the caller passes to the next call. A length above max (or MaxData when max is 0) fails with ErrTooLarge before the data is read: the stream cannot be resynchronised and should be closed. io.EOF is returned as is when the stream ends between packets, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF inside one.
